label: Words 1–100
words: you (usually when one doesn't know the person)
ありがとうございます
ありがとうございます
give (receiver is not in the speaker's group)
give (receiver is in the speaker's group)
you (to someone of equal or lower status)

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: この本、どう思いますか。
lines.translation: What do you think of this book?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 面白いと思います。でも、ちょっと高いですね。
lines.translation: I think it’s interesting. But it’s a little expensive.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: そうですね。あの本はどうですか。
lines.translation: That’s true. How about that book over there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: あの本の方がいいと思います。
lines.translation: I think that book would be better.

questions.question: What concern does B have about the first book?
choices: It costs a little too much
It is not interesting at all
questions.explanation: Focus: 高い (expensive), ちょっと (a little). B finds the book interesting but a little expensive. Extra connector: でも means but.

questions.situation: Looking at a tall building · Two friends

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: あの高い建物は何ですか。
lines.translation: What is that tall building over there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 学校です。この町で一番高い建物です。
lines.translation: It’s a school. It’s the tallest building in this town.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 本当ですか。前に行って、見たいです。
lines.translation: Really? I want to go in front of it and have a look.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: いいですね。行きましょう。
lines.translation: Sounds good. Let’s go.

questions.question: What is the tallest building in the town?
questions.explanation: Focus: 町 (town), 高い (tall), 一番 (most), 本当 (really), 前 (front). Extra word: 建物 (たてもの) means building. 一番高い means tallest here; 見たい means want to see.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: もう日本語の勉強をしましたか。
lines.translation: Have you already studied Japanese?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: はい、もうしました。
lines.translation: Yes, I already have.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: もう家に帰りますか。
lines.translation: Are you going home already?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: いいえ、ここで友達を待ちます。
lines.translation: No, I’ll wait here for a friend.

questions.question: What will B do now?
choices: Start studying for the first time today
questions.explanation: Focus: もう (already). B has already studied, but will wait here for a friend rather than go home.

questions.situation: Listening again · A learner and a teacher

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: ちょっと分かりません。もう一度言ってください。
lines.translation: I don’t quite understand. Please say it once more.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: はい、ゆっくり言います。ここに立ってください。
lines.translation: Yes, I’ll say it slowly. Please stand here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: ここですか。
lines.translation: Here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: はい、そうです。
lines.translation: Yes, that’s right.

questions.question: What instruction does B repeat?
questions.explanation: Focus: もう (again), ちょっと (a little), 立つ (stand). Extra expression: もう一度 (もういちど) means once more. 立ってください is the polite request form of 立つ.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: お父さんはこの町が好きですか。
lines.translation: Does your father like this town?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: はい、父はこの町が大好きです。
lines.translation: Yes, my father loves this town.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: お母さんも好きですか。
lines.translation: Does your mother like it too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: はい、母も大好きです。
lines.translation: Yes, my mother loves it too.

questions.question: Who loves the town?
questions.explanation: Focus: 父 (my father), 母 (my mother), 大好き (love), 町 (town). Extra polite family terms: お父さん and お母さん are used here for someone else’s parents.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: その本、どうしますか。
lines.translation: What will you do with that book?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 友達にあげます。
lines.translation: I’ll give it to a friend.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: お父さんにあげますか。
lines.translation: Will you give it to your father?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: いいえ、父ではありません。友達にあげます。
lines.translation: No, not my father. I’ll give it to a friend.

questions.question: Who will receive B’s book?
questions.explanation: Focus: あげる (give to someone), 父 (my father). 友達にあげます identifies the friend as the recipient. お父さん is a polite term used here for B’s father.

questions.situation: A book from a friend · Two classmates

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: その本は面白いですか。
lines.translation: Is that book interesting?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: はい。友達がくれました。
lines.translation: Yes. A friend gave it to me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: いいですね。日本語の本ですか。
lines.translation: That’s nice. Is it a Japanese-language book?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: はい。この本が大好きです。
lines.translation: Yes. I love this book.

questions.question: Who gave the book to whom?
choices: B gave it to a friend
The teacher gave it to A
A friend gave it to B
questions.explanation: Focus: くれる (someone gives to me/us), 大好き (love). 友達がくれました means a friend gave it to the speaker, B. Listen for the direction of giving.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 昨日、先生に何をもらいましたか。
lines.translation: What did you receive from the teacher yesterday?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 本をもらいました。
lines.translation: I received a book.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: もう見ましたか。
lines.translation: Have you looked at it already?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: はい、もう見ました。面白い本です。
lines.translation: Yes, I already have. It’s an interesting book.

questions.question: What did B receive from the teacher?
questions.explanation: Focus: もらう (receive), もう (already). 先生にもらいました means received from the teacher; B received a book and has already looked at it.

questions.situation: Something in a bag · Two friends

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: その中の物は何ですか。
lines.translation: What is the object inside that?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: 本です。母にもらいました。
lines.translation: It’s a book. I received it from my mother.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: ちょっと見てもいいですか。
lines.translation: May I take a quick look?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: はい、いいですよ。
lines.translation: Yes, of course.

questions.question: Where did B get the object inside?
questions.explanation: Focus: 中 (inside), 物 (object), 母 (my mother), もらう (receive). B received the book from their mother. 見てもいいですか is a request for permission to look.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 君は日本語ができる？
lines.translation: Can you speak Japanese?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: うん、ちょっとできるよ。
lines.translation: Yeah, a little.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 本当？みんなの前で話せる？
lines.translation: Really? Can you speak in front of everyone?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: うん、ゆっくり話すよ。
lines.translation: Yeah, I’ll speak slowly.

questions.question: What does B say about their Japanese?
choices: B can use a little and will speak slowly
B refuses to speak to anyone
questions.explanation: Focus: 君 (you, familiar), 出来る／できる (can), 本当 (really), 前 (in front). Extra words: うん is casual yes; みんな means everyone. 話せる is the potential form of 話す. 君 suits some familiar relationships; avoid using it as a default polite you.
